text: On October twenty-fifth, twenty seventeen, a woman boarded a flight from Sofia to Athens.
visual: STORY S5. Empty airport departure hall at dawn. Slow push on the departure board; one row (code text) reads SOFIA → ATHENS. No people.

text: Then she vanished.
visual: STORY S5. Same board. The SOFIA → ATHENS row flips to blank. Empty gate seats hold.

text: Her company, OneCoin, had taken in more than four billion dollars.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam. "$4B+" in red counts up. Label: TAKEN IN, Q4 2014–Q4 2016.

text: It came from at least three and a half million people.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam. "3.5M" in red. Label: VICTIMS (AT LEAST).

text: People like Rosa, a tailor who sews other people's wedding dresses.
visual: STORY S1. Rosa at her sewing machine, tape measure round her neck, guiding white lace under the needle.

text: Today, the woman on that flight is on the F.B.I.'s Ten Most Wanted list.
visual: EVIDENCE filing card (no photo, text only): FBI TEN MOST WANTED FUGITIVES. Name typed in. Source line: FBI, 30 JUN 2022.

text: So how do you sell millions of people a coin that never existed?
visual: Code-built: a single gold coin on navy grid; its fill drains away, leaving only a dotted outline. Slow push.

text: Rosa runs a small tailoring shop with one sewing machine and one dream.
visual: CHAPTER CARD 2 s: PART 1 / THE DREAM. Then STORY S1 wide, morning: Rosa threading the machine, dress form beside her.

text: She is saving for her daughter's university, one hem at a time.
visual: STORY S1 close. Rosa slips folded banknotes into a plain envelope marked UNI (code text).

text: It's twenty sixteen, and Bitcoin keeps turning up on the evening news.
visual: STORY S1. Small TV on the shelf shows a gold line climbing (code graphic). Rosa glances up from her hemming.

text: Its price has climbed from a few cents to hundreds of dollars.
visual: EVIDENCE chart: gold line draws itself upward, months on axis, tag "shape illustrative". Label: BITCOIN, FROM CENTS TO HUNDREDS OF DOLLARS (words, no figure).

text: If you missed that ride, you would badly want a second ticket.
visual: STORY S1. Rosa looks from the TV to her thin UNI envelope, thinking expression.

text: Then her friend Dee sends her a link to a live webinar.
visual: STORY S2, night. Rosa's phone lights up on the kitchen table; message bubble (code): "Rosa you HAVE to see this" with a link.

text: The hosts on screen are bright, fast and very, very excited.
visual: Laptop screen (code UI): webinar grid of smiling tiles, Dee in one tile with her gimbal phone, gold confetti graphic.

text: Their pitch is simple: get in early, and this goes bigger than Bitcoin.
visual: Laptop close: banner graphic (code) BIGGER THAN BITCOIN pulsing gold.

text: It's called OneCoin.
visual: Laptop close: a gold coin logo-free graphic with the word ONECOIN (code text, generic type).

text: It was founded in twenty fourteen and is run from Sofia, Bulgaria.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "OneCoin Ltd. founded 2014, based in Sofia, Bulgaria". PARAPHRASED FROM: US DOJ SDNY.

text: Its founder is sold as a genius, with genuine degrees on every slide.
visual: Laptop: webinar slide (code) with diploma icons and the words "Dr." and "PhD". No photo, no face.

text: There's even a magazine cover, which was really a paid advertisement.
visual: EVIDENCE paper card: a logo-free magazine-cover frame; the corner peels back to reveal the word ADVERTISEMENT. RECREATED FROM: BBC.

text: Strangely, Rosa can't buy OneCoins directly, because nobody sells them.
visual: STORY S2. Rosa frowning at the laptop, pen in hand, notepad with a question mark.

text: OneCoin sells education packages: online courses, bundled with promotional tokens.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "packages which contained online educational courses bundled with promotional tokens". RECREATED FROM: Singapore Police Force.

text: The tokens, she's told, can be used to mine brand new coins.
visual: Laptop: promo-style animation (code) of server racks labelled MINING POOL, gold lights blinking.

text: Packages run from a hundred and forty euros to a hundred and eighteen thousand.
visual: EVIDENCE bar card: two bars, small and towering. Labels "€140" and "€118,000". Source: BBC.

text: Rosa starts with a small package, just to see what happens.
visual: STORY S2. Rosa clicks BUY on the laptop (code button); the UNI envelope beside her looks a little thinner.

text: Then she watches the balance on her account page go up.
visual: Laptop dashboard (code): coin balance and euro value tick upward in gold.

text: And up.
visual: Same dashboard: the euro value jumps again; gold glow.

text: So she slides the whole university envelope into OneCoin as well.
visual: STORY S2 close. Rosa's hand pushes the UNI envelope across the table towards the laptop.

text: Dee's upline is Victor, who hosts OneCoin seminars in hotel ballrooms.
visual: STORY S3. Victor on stage, gold tie, clicker raised, slide behind him blank-gold. Distant crowd shapes.

text: Victor says the real money comes from bringing other people in.
visual: S3. Victor clicks; slide becomes a downline tree diagram (code), one node at the top, many below.

text: Every friend you sign up who buys a package earns you a commission.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: tree nodes light gold one by one; a small coin drops into the top node each time.

text: It feels like a Black Friday queue, and nobody asks what's on sale.
visual: STORY S3 wide. Crowd shapes queue at ballroom doors under gold banners (no logos).

text: Rosa signs up her sister, then two regulars from her shop.
visual: STORY S1. Rosa shows her phone to two customers at the counter; both lean in, smiling.

text: In June twenty sixteen, the founder headlines a huge event at Wembley Arena.
visual: STORY S3 variant, arena. Distant crowd, gold sparks, centre spotlight EMPTY (founder never drawn).

text: On stage she welcomes the press nickname for OneCoin: the Bitcoin killer.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "…supposed to be the bitcoin killer. Well, I must say I like it." RECREATED FROM: FBI video transcript.

text: Rosa isn't scheming at all; she believes every single word.
visual: STORY S2. Rosa watching the event stream on her laptop, hopeful expression, hand on heart.

text: But what exactly is Rosa's hard-earned money really buying?
visual: STORY S2 night. Rosa alone, laptop glow on her face, the gold balance glowing. Slow push-in.

text: Here's how the OneCoin machine actually worked, one step at a time.
visual: CHAPTER CARD 2 s: PART 2 / THE MACHINE. Then EVIDENCE board: three empty boxes slide in, left to right.

text: You buy a package, and the package comes loaded with tokens.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: box PACKAGE → arrow → TOKENS.

text: Those tokens are then converted into OneCoins sitting in your account.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: TOKENS → ONECOINS; the third box fills with gold coins.

text: Promoters said powerful computers in mining pools created those coins.
visual: Promo-style animation (code): server racks in a dark hall, gold lights blinking. Label: AS PROMOTED.

text: Prosecutors say there were no mining pools and no computers at all.
visual: Same racks: lights switch off one by one; off-white stamp NO MINING POOLS. Source: US DOJ SDNY, 12 SEP 2023.

text: In one email, the founder told her co-founder they were not mining actually.
visual: EVIDENCE email card (code): header FROM: IGNATOVA / TO: GREENWOOD; body blurred except "not mining actually" highlighted amber. RECREATED FROM: US DOJ SDNY.
say: In one email, the founder told her co-founder they were not mining, actually.

text: The co-founder, Sebastian Greenwood, ran the global sales network.
visual: EVIDENCE name card: SEBASTIAN GREENWOOD — CO-FOUNDER, MASTER DISTRIBUTOR. No photo.

text: He took a cut of every month's sales, anywhere in the world.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: world map dots send thin gold lines to one node labelled CO-FOUNDER.

text: That cut added up to more than three hundred million dollars, prosecutors said.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam: "$300M+" gold. Label: CO-FOUNDER'S CUT (5% OF MONTHLY SALES). Source: US DOJ SDNY, 12 SEP 2023.

text: And the cash behind every commission came from the next wave of buyers.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: new nodes join the bottom of the downline tree; gold flows upward from them to the top.

text: So who decided what one OneCoin was actually worth?
visual: STORY S2. Rosa squinting at the dashboard's euro value, pen tapping her lip.

text: The company did.
visual: Code shot: an anonymous hand (charcoal cuff) turns a big dial labelled PRICE.

text: OneCoin claimed its price came from market supply and demand.
visual: EVIDENCE chart: SUPPLY and DEMAND curves cross, label "AS CLAIMED".

text: In fact, prosecutors say, the company simply set the price itself.
visual: Same chart: curves fade; the hand turns the PRICE dial again and the needle climbs.

text: It went from fifty euro cents to twenty-nine euros ninety-five.
visual: EVIDENCE chart: gold staircase line, peak marked. "€0.50 → €29.95". Source: US DOJ SDNY.

text: And it never fell.
visual: Same staircase: every step only rises; no dip anywhere.

text: By around March twenty fifteen, the founders were handing out coins they called fake.
visual: EVIDENCE email/spreadsheet card (code): columns MINED COINS · MINED COINS (REAL) · FAKE COINS; FAKE COINS highlighted amber. RECREATED FROM: US DOJ SDNY.

text: Their own spreadsheets had separate lines for mined coins and fake coins.
visual: Same card: the cursor runs down the FAKE COINS row; values blurred.

text: That's not a market; that's a price tag with a progress bar.
visual: Rosa's dashboard (code): the euro value replaced by a loading bar filling left to right.

text: Then there's the blockchain, the public record behind real cryptocurrencies.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: a chain of blocks; identical copies blink on across a world map.
say: Then there's the block chain, the public record behind real cryptocurrencies.

text: With Bitcoin, you can check every single transaction on that shared record yourself.
visual: Same diagram: a magnifier sweeps over the blocks; each lights as it passes.

text: Thousands of independent computers keep identical copies, so nobody can quietly rewrite it.
visual: Same diagram: dozens of identical ledgers glow on the map; one tries to change a block and turns red, the rest stay gold.

text: OneCoin said it had a blockchain too, but a private one.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: a single block locked inside a steel safe.
say: OneCoin said it had a block chain too, but a private one.

text: Investors, an F.B.I. agent later said, were just asked to trust OneCoin.
visual: STORY S3. Victor on stage, palms open; slide behind him (code): TRUST US.

text: Theo, a developer who builds these systems, isn't buying any of it.
visual: STORY S4. Theo at his three monitors late at night, red pen behind his ear, arms folded.

text: He keeps posting one plain question online: where is the ledger?
visual: S4 monitor close (code): forum thread title WHERE IS THE LEDGER? with a blinking cursor.

text: He even offers to review OneCoin's code for free, but nobody sends it.
visual: S4. Theo's email (code) "Happy to audit your ledger, no charge" — reply area stays empty; cursor blinks.

text: In Rosa's group chat, people like Theo are simply called haters.
visual: Phone screen (code): group chat, message "Ignore the haters!! 🙌" with many likes. (BBC: critics were called 'haters'.)

text: In October twenty sixteen, a real blockchain expert got an odd job offer.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card slides in: "Crypto start-up seeks chief technical officer". RECREATED FROM: BBC.
say: In October twenty sixteen, a real block chain expert got an odd job offer.

text: A cryptocurrency start-up from Bulgaria needed a chief technical officer.
visual: Same card: job listing frame (code) CTO WANTED · SOFIA · APARTMENT + CAR.

text: His first job, the recruiter explained, would be to build a blockchain.
visual: Card highlight amber: "they need a blockchain".
say: His first job, the recruiter explained, would be to build a block chain.

text: Because the company running a cryptocurrency didn't actually have one.
visual: Card highlight amber: "They don't have a blockchain today."

text: The company was OneCoin, and the expert turned the job down.
visual: Card: off-white stamp DECLINED lands on the listing.

text: Meanwhile, Rosa's balance keeps climbing, and so does her confidence.
visual: STORY S1. Rosa hemming a wedding dress, smiling; phone propped up showing the rising gold balance.

text: Every number she sees lives on OneCoin's own website, and nowhere else.
visual: Phone close (code): the dashboard; the frame pulls back to show it is the only window, surrounded by navy emptiness.

text: Victor's slides promise an exchange is coming, where coins will become cash.
visual: STORY S3. Victor clicks; slide (code) shows EXCHANGE · COMING SOON with a countdown clock.

text: It's the Wizard of Oz: the show works until someone pulls the curtain.
visual: STORY S3. Victor mid-pitch; the heavy curtain behind him parts a little, revealing a plain desk with one laptop.

text: Now the twist, and it comes straight from the prosecutors' own files.
visual: EVIDENCE board: a sealed folder labelled COURT EXHIBIT slides in and opens. (1 s near-silence before this line.)

text: On August ninth, twenty fourteen, the founders discussed an exit strategy.
visual: EVIDENCE email card dated 9 AUG 2014, subject line "exit strategy". RECREATED FROM: US DOJ SDNY.

text: That's months before OneCoin even claimed to mine its very first coin.
visual: EVIDENCE timeline: dot 9 AUG 2014 (exit email) … dot JAN 2015 ("first coin mined", as claimed on stage).

text: The first option on her list read: take the money and run.
visual: Email card close: highlight amber "Take the money and run and blame someone else for this . . ."

text: And blame someone else.
visual: Highlight extends across "blame someone else"; hold.

text: Prosecutors say OneCoin was built as a fraud from day one.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "conceived of ... as a fraud from day one". PARAPHRASED FROM: US DOJ SDNY, 12 SEP 2023.

text: So when the music finally stops, who gets out first?
visual: STORY S3. Victor's stage: the speaker stacks go dark one by one; the crowd shapes stay. Slow push.

text: The first crack is a warning from Britain's financial regulator.
visual: CHAPTER CARD 2 s: PART 3 / THE FALL. Then EVIDENCE headline card: "Beware trading virtual currencies with OneCoin". RECREATED FROM: BBC (FCA notice).

text: In September twenty sixteen, the F.C.A. told consumers to be wary of OneCoin.
visual: Same card, dateline SEP 2016 added; small grey label WARNING ≠ FINE.

text: To be clear, that was a warning, not a fine.
visual: Close on the grey label WARNING ≠ FINE.

text: Less than a year later, the notice was quietly taken down.
visual: The headline card fades to blank paper; only the dateline remains.

text: Promoters waved that removal around like a clean bill of health.
visual: STORY S3. Victor beams, pointing his clicker at a slide (code) showing a blank page with a gold tick.

text: Meanwhile, the exchange where you could finally turn coins into cash keeps slipping.
visual: Rosa's dashboard (code): a CASH OUT button, greyed, label COMING SOON.

text: Rosa asks Dee when she can withdraw, and Dee keeps saying soon.
visual: STORY S2. Rosa typing on her phone; reply bubble (code) from Dee: "Soon!! Be patient".

text: Theo, meanwhile, sends Rosa one careful link after another.
visual: STORY S4. Theo at his desk pressing send; cut to Rosa's phone filling with link previews.

text: A real investor from Glasgow, Jen McAdam, started asking the same question.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "Investor asks her group leaders: is there a blockchain?" RECREATED FROM: BBC. No photo.

text: She had put in ten thousand euros, and her family a quarter million.
visual: EVIDENCE stat card: "€10,000" and "€250,000" stacked, red. Label: OWN + FAMILY. Source: BBC.

text: In April twenty seventeen, a voicemail from her group finally answered her.
visual: EVIDENCE card: a voicemail waveform graphic (code) with dateline APR 2017 in the source line.

text: Their blockchain, it said, was a SQL server with a database.
visual: Card highlight amber: "a SQL server with a database". RECREATED FROM: BBC, 24 NOV 2019.
say: Their block chain, it said, was an S.Q.L. server with a database.

text: In other words, a record the company could change whenever it liked.
visual: EVIDENCE: a spreadsheet grid (code); a cursor overwrites a number, then another.

text: Then, in October twenty seventeen, the founder fails to show up in Lisbon.
visual: STORY S3 variant. Empty stage, empty spotlight; a programme card on a seat reads LISBON (code).

text: Around the same time, prosecutors in New York charged her with fraud.
visual: EVIDENCE filing card: UNITED STATES v. IGNATOVA — CHARGED. Source line: FBI, 12 OCT 2017.

text: On October twenty-fifth, she flew from Sofia to Athens.
visual: STORY S5. The airport departure board again, SOFIA → ATHENS row lit.

text: She has not been seen in public since.
visual: S5. The row flips to blank; slow push on the empty gate.

text: Gone.
visual: S5. Hold on empty seats, pale dawn light. (emotional hold)

text: The F.B.I. believes she travels with armed guards and may have had surgery.
visual: EVIDENCE filing card (text only, no photo): MAY TRAVEL WITH ARMED GUARDS · MAY HAVE ALTERED HER APPEARANCE. Source: FBI Ten Most Wanted page.

text: Her brother, Konstantin Ignatov, rose to lead the company after she disappeared.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "Brother rises to top leadership by mid-2018". PARAPHRASED FROM: US DOJ SDNY, 8 MAR 2019.
say: Her brother, Konstantin Ig-NAH-tov, rose to lead the company after she disappeared.

text: In Las Vegas, members asked him when they could finally cash out.
visual: STORY. Ballroom stage (S3 variant) with an EMPTY microphone stand, casino-coloured light. No person.

text: He reportedly said: if you are here to cash out, leave this room now.
visual: EVIDENCE filing card with the quote; RECREATED FROM: US DOJ SDNY, 8 MAR 2019.

text: In March twenty nineteen, the F.B.I. arrested him at Los Angeles airport.
visual: STORY S5 variant. Airport gate sign (code) flips from BOARDING to CLOSED. No people.

text: Rosa reads the news on her phone in the shop and sits down.
visual: STORY S1, dusk. Rosa sinks onto a stool, phone in hand, the half-finished wedding dress behind her.

text: Her dashboard still shows a healthy balance in bright gold numbers.
visual: Phone close (code): the gold balance still glowing; a faint red line strikes through it.

text: Like the band on the Titanic, the dashboard just kept playing.
visual: Phone close: the numbers keep ticking up while the shop lights behind dim to navy.

text: The hardest call is to her sister, who only joined because Rosa asked.
visual: STORY S1, dusk. Rosa on the phone, eyes closed, tape measure clutched in her other hand.

text: Dee, who recruited half her street, now avoids her own neighbours.
visual: STORY. Dee at her front window (S2-style night interior), curtain half drawn, gimbal phone face-down on the sill.

text: She isn't alone: investors came from a hundred and seventy-five countries.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam: "175" in red. Label: COUNTRIES. Source: BBC, 25 SEP 2019.

text: In Uganda, one young man sold his brothers' three goats to buy in.
visual: STORY. Three goats in a green field at dusk (no people). Headline card corner: RECREATED FROM: BBC.

text: Then he persuaded his mother to put the family's savings in too.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "Family savings meant for a maize store went into OneCoin". RECREATED FROM: BBC.

text: The courts did eventually catch up with the people around the founder.
visual: STORY S6. Courthouse exterior, overcast; slow push up the empty steps.

text: Co-founder Sebastian Greenwood was sentenced to twenty years in prison.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam: "20 YEARS". Label: SEBASTIAN GREENWOOD, CO-FOUNDER. Source: US DOJ SDNY / Reuters, 12 SEP 2023.

text: Mark Scott, a lawyer who laundered OneCoin money, was sentenced to ten.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam: "10 YEARS". Label: MARK SCOTT, LAWYER. Source: US DOJ SDNY / Reuters, 25 JAN 2024.

text: Irina Dilkinska, the so-called head of legal and compliance, got four.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam: "4 YEARS". Label: IRINA DILKINSKA, "HEAD OF LEGAL AND COMPLIANCE". Source: US DOJ SDNY / Reuters, 3 APR 2024.
say: Irina Dil-KIN-ska, the so-called head of legal and compliance, got four.

text: Konstantin cooperated with prosecutors and was sentenced to time already served.
visual: EVIDENCE name card: KONSTANTIN IGNATOV — TIME SERVED. Source: SDNY court letter / Bloomberg Law.

text: British police said they found no UK assets to compensate British investors.
visual: EVIDENCE headline card: "unable to identify UK-based assets". RECREATED FROM: BBC (City of London Police).
say: British police said they found no U.K. assets to compensate British investors.

text: So could Rosa have seen it coming, and could you?
visual: STORY S1, dusk. Rosa at the shop window, her reflection in the glass. Slow push.

text: Here are three red flags you can spot without any computer science degree.
visual: CHAPTER CARD 2 s: PART 4 / THE LESSON. Then EVIDENCE board: three face-down cards labelled 1, 2, 3.

text: Red flag one: the price of the thing only ever goes up.
visual: Card 1 flips: PRICE ONLY GOES UP, with a small gold staircase line.

text: Real markets wobble, but OneCoin's price, set by the company, never fell.
visual: EVIDENCE: two mini charts side by side, a jagged line ("real market, illustrative") and the smooth OneCoin staircase.

text: Red flag two: you are not allowed to check it for yourself.
visual: Card 2 flips: YOU CAN'T VERIFY IT, with a padlock icon.

text: A real cryptocurrency lets anyone inspect its ledger, without asking anybody's permission.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: the magnifier sweeps a public chain of blocks again.

text: If the only answer you get is trust us, that is your answer.
visual: STORY S3. Victor's TRUST US slide; a small red stamp RED FLAG lands on it.

text: Red flag three: the money comes mostly from recruiting, not from a product.
visual: Card 3 flips: PAID TO RECRUIT, with the downline tree icon.

text: If the main way to earn is signing up your sister, step back.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: Rosa's downline tree; the node labelled SISTER glows, then dims.

text: In Singapore, one OneCoin promoter who ran recruiting seminars got six months in prison.
visual: EVIDENCE stat slam: "6 MONTHS". Label: ONECOIN PROMOTER, SINGAPORE (2021). Source: Singapore Police Force, 20 JAN 2021.

text: Victim and recruiter can be the same person, and that's how it spreads.
visual: EVIDENCE diagram: the downline tree; Rosa's node is both lit gold (recruiter) and outlined red (victim).

text: Sherlock Holmes would start with the most boring question: where is the ledger?
visual: Code shot: a magnifying glass and an open notebook; handwriting (code) reads WHERE IS THE LEDGER? (no character image).

text: Remember our question: how do you sell a coin that never existed?
visual: The dotted gold coin outline from the cold open returns to centre frame.

text: You sell a feeling, a family, and a number that only goes up.
visual: Triptych: Rosa's group chat, Victor's stage, the rising gold dashboard.

text: Then you make very sure that nobody is ever allowed to check.
visual: The steel safe with the private block slams shut.

text: In April twenty twenty-six, the Justice Department finally opened a fund for victims.
visual: EVIDENCE filing card: VICTIM COMPENSATION PROCESS OPENS (paraphrased), dateline 13 APR 2026.

text: It holds just over forty million dollars, against more than four billion taken.
visual: EVIDENCE bar comparison: tiny gold bar $40M+ beside a towering red bar $4B+.

text: That's about one cent back for every dollar.
visual: Code-built: a single small copper cent beside a full dollar bill shape on the navy grid. Label: ~1 CENT PER $1 (computed from $40M / $4B).

text: Rosa filed her claim before the June deadline, and now she waits.
visual: STORY S2, night. Rosa at her kitchen table, signing a paper form beside the UNI envelope.

text: Rosa still runs her shop, and she still saves, one hem at a time.
visual: STORY S1, morning. Rosa sewing; a new UNI envelope on the counter.

text: But now, before she trusts any number, she asks to see the ledger.
visual: STORY S1. Rosa pins Theo's printed page WHERE IS THE LEDGER? to the wall above her machine.

text: Next time a number only goes up, will you ask to see it?
visual: STORY S1. Close on the pinned page; slow push.

text: Next time on Wisdrop: another money crime hiding behind the hype.
visual: END CARD: navy board, NEXT CASE (title TBD by owner), WISDROP corner mark. Music out.
